<pre>Transmission of material in this release is embargoed until USDL 26-1687 8:30 a.m. (ET) Friday, November 13, 2026 Technical information: (202) 691-7705 * ppi-info@bls.gov * www.bls.gov/ppi Media contact: (202) 691-5902 * PressOffice@bls.gov PRODUCER PRICE INDEXES - OCTOBER 2026 The Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3 percent in October, seasonally adjusted, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. Final demand prices advanced 1.4 percent in September and 0.4 percent in August. (See table A.) On an unadjusted basis, the index for final demand increased 6.5 percent for the 12 months ended in October, the largest 12-month rise since moving up 7.4 percent in November 2022. Leading the October advance in final demand prices, the index for final demand goods increased 0.5 percent. Prices for final demand services moved up 0.2 percent. The index for final demand less foods, energy, and trade services rose 0.5 percent in October, the same as in September. For the 12 months ended in October, prices for final demand less foods, energy, and trade services advanced 4.9 percent. Final Demand Final demand goods: The index for final demand goods increased 0.5 percent in October following a 2.5-percent rise in September. Over 60 percent of the advance in October is attributable to prices for final demand goods less foods and energy, which moved up 0.5 percent. The index for final demand foods increased 1.3 percent. In contrast, prices for final demand energy edged down 0.1 percent. For the 12 months ended in October, the index for final demand goods increased 10.2 percent, the largest 12-month rise since advancing 10.5 percent in October 2022. Product detail: Within the index for final demand goods in October, prices for basic organic chemicals advanced 3.9 percent. The indexes for fresh and dry vegetables; gas fuels; aeronautical, nautical, and navigational instruments; jet fuel; and processed young chickens also moved higher. (See table 2.) Conversely, diesel fuel prices fell 7.9 percent. The indexes for pork and for passenger cars also declined. Final demand services: The index for final demand services moved up 0.2 percent in October, the fifth consecutive advance. Three-fourths of the October rise can be traced to a 2.0-percent increase in prices for final demand transportation and warehousing services. The index for final demand services less trade, transportation, and warehousing advanced 0.2 percent. In contrast, margins for final demand trade services decreased 0.2 percent. Product detail: Over 80 percent of the October increase in the index for final demand services is attributable to prices for truck transportation of freight, which rose 3.9 percent. The indexes for fuels and lubricants retailing; health, beauty, and optical goods retailing; food and alcohol wholesaling; hospital outpatient care; and traveler accommodation services also moved higher. Conversely, margins for machinery and vehicle wholesaling fell 4.2 percent. Prices for system software publishing and for airline passenger services also declined.</pre>
